title: CSSTs: A Dynamic Data Structure for Partial Orders in Concurrent Execution Analysis
problem: Vector Clocks require O(n) time to insert and propagate each new ordering in a partial order (where n is trace size) and cannot handle deletion of orderings, limiting scalability of concurrent execution analysis.
motivation: Scalability of dynamic program analysis for detecting bugs in concurrent programs depends on efficient maintenance of partial order dependencies between trace events.
method: CSSTs are a novel dynamic data structure that replaces Vector Clocks for representing partial orders in concurrent execution traces. The structure supports both insertion and deletion of ordering constraints more efficiently than the O(n) complexity of Vector Clocks, enabling scalable non-streaming dynamic analysis.
key_novelty: A dynamic data structure (CSST) that efficiently maintains partial orders while supporting deletion operations, unlike Vector Clocks.
contributions: Identifies efficiency limitations of Vector Clocks for concurrent execution analysis
Proposes CSSTs as an alternative data structure for partial order management
Supports both insertion and deletion of ordering constraints
Enables scalable analysis of non-streaming concurrent program traces

metrics.other: Vector Clocks: O(n) per operation; CSST performance not specified

primary_theme: efficient data structures for concurrent program analysis
